methodology_note: Same fully-itemized convention as V2 (flat sum: total_scored_items = match+sem_eq+missing+incorrect+extra, percentage = (match+sem_eq)/total_scored_items, extras INCLUDED in the denominator). V3 genuinely surfaced 4 new, accurate commercial-clause rows Deep Verify's report never had (Payment Withholding/Setoff, Pricing Escalation, Assignment, Governing Law & Dispute) -- under this flat-sum convention, each additional accurate-but-extra row counts AGAINST the percentage, producing a counterintuitive result (the score goes DOWN even though real content went up). Per instruction 13 ('do not alter denominators ... to achieve 90%'), this report does not suppress or reweight that -- both the flat-sum number and a required-items-only number (denominator excludes EXTRA_NOT_REQUIRED entirely) are reported below, fully labeled, so the artifact of this specific convention is visible rather than hidden.

insurance_root_cause_investigation.evidence: Direct text search of Appendix G's parsed document confirms the genuine $3,000,000 CGL / Errors & Omissions / Workplace Safety and Insurance clause text exists at character offset ~19807-21375 of a 32,452-char document. Fast Analysis's own chunker splits this document into [23904, 8326, 319]-char pieces at FAST_MAX_CHUNK_CHARS=24000; the Insurance text falls inside chunk 0 (0-23904 chars), which is exactly the chunk that hit max_tokens in both V1 and V2. The COMMERCIAL_ONLY schema already declares INSURANCE as a valid clause_kind -- this was never a schema or model-omission problem.
insurance_root_cause_investigation.fix_applied: None needed beyond the general split-on-truncation mechanism -- confirmed this run's split of chunk 0 (23904 -> ~11786/~12312 chars) let one half (Appendix G's own separate second truncating chunk, 8326 chars, split into ~4082/4438 chars) complete cleanly and surface the Insurance content.
insurance_root_cause_investigation.v2_prompt_experiment_status: REVERTED (per instruction 9) -- it added 3 extra calls in V2 and did not recover Insurance; the split mechanism fixed the real cause instead.

abnormally_low_pricing_root_cause_invest.evidence: Direct text search across the master RFP, Appendix E, and Appendix G confirms the 'abnormally low' pricing-consequence language (explanation requirement, performance-bond consequence) exists ONLY in the master RFP, at character offset ~25026-25609 of a 52,145-char document -- NOT in Appendix E as originally assumed in V2. This falls inside the master RFP's own chunk index 1 (21,804-44,651 chars), the exact same chunk responsible for the still-unresolved ambiguity gap. Separately, the IDENTITY_EVAL_REQ schema's `requirements` family was restricted to exactly 2 topics (category scope, submission mechanics) -- 'abnormally low pricing' fit neither, so even an untruncated read would not have requested it.
abnormally_low_pricing_root_cause_invest.fix_applied: Widened the EXISTING requirements-topic filter from 2 to 3 topics (adding pricing-evaluation-consequence rules) -- a minimal, single-clause addition to an already-declared family in an already-existing route/task, not a new family or route. Confirmed in the prompt text via test_identity_eval_req_prompt_now_requests_pricing_consequence_topic.
abnormally_low_pricing_root_cause_invest.result_this_run: Still MISSING. The schema now requests it, but the master RFP's chunk 1 split (into ~10,191/~12,656-char halves) still truncated on both halves before reaching the requirements array (which is the LAST family in the JSON schema's field order) -- a newly identified, general risk: truncation disproportionately harms whichever family is requested last in the schema, regardless of where the underlying fact sits in the source text.

d1_d2_d3_weight_extraction_regression_th.severity: material but NOT V3-code-caused -- fully investigated
d1_d2_d3_weight_extraction_regression_th.finding: This specific live run's raw extraction for D1, D2, D3 (all 3 rated-criteria forms) and the B1-3/C1-3 batch call returned every evaluation_criteria weight value as null, despite none of those calls truncating (all ended with stop_reason=end_turn, parse_status=COMPLETE except the batch call which did truncate this run, unlike V1/V2). This is pure live model-output variance between API calls on different days -- V3 did not touch the EVAL_ONLY route, its schema, or D1/D2/D3 routing/chunking at all.
d1_d2_d3_weight_extraction_regression_th.impact: None visible in the delivered PDF: the pre-existing (v1) all-or-nothing safety-net fallback (`if not C.EVAL_WEIGHTS: C.EVAL_WEIGHTS = DEEP.EVAL_WEIGHTS`) correctly triggered because ALL THREE categories came back empty simultaneously, substituting the validated, correct Deep Verify weight tables. The rendered report is fully correct.
d1_d2_d3_weight_extraction_regression_th.reliability_risk_identified: The current required-fields check for the EVAL_ONLY route only verifies that `evaluation_criteria` is a non-empty list -- it does not check that individual entries carry a non-null `weight`. A response with well-formed but entirely null-valued entries is treated as complete and never triggers any retry or recovery path. This run's fallback saved the report because ALL THREE categories failed identically; a run where only ONE category degraded this way would silently produce a partial, non-Deep-Verify-matching weight table with no safety net (the fallback is all-or-nothing across the whole EVAL_WEIGHTS dict, not per-category). This is a genuine, newly-identified robustness gap, explicitly out of V3's authorized scope to fix (no new recovery mechanism was authorized beyond bounded split-on-truncation) -- flagged here for a future iteration rather than fixed unilaterally.
